messages:
support_jane: Raising an escalation — acme-co seeing P99 latency spike on /v1/generate-toolcall after 2026-03-14 deploy. P95 from ~120ms -> 420ms, P99 to ~1.9s.
maria: Which customers/routes are impacted? Any recent changes?
support_jane: Only requests that include inline tool definitions with large JSON schemas. Logs show repeated entries: 'schema-validator: validation_time_ms=350' on slow traces.
kevin: assigning to eng-runtime, pinging @taylan oncall.
taylan: taking. Can you paste a raw request we can repro with? :mag:
support_jane: sanitized repro curl below:

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate-toolcall \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
 -d '{"input":"What's the price for model-x?","tools":[{"name":"price_lookup","description":"Lookup prices","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"item":{"type":"string"},"filters":{"type":"object","properties":{"region":{"type":"string"},"currency":{"type":"string"},"attributes":{"type":"object","properties":{"color":{"type":"string"},"size":{"type":"string"}}}}}}}]}'
```

support_jane: Repro steps: hit with 10 concurrent requests; p99 climbs once tool-router CPU > 75% and queue latency rises.

taylan: I instrumented traces. Two hotspots: (1) JSON schema validator runs synchronously inside tool-router worker thread, (2) router queueing increases tail latency when validator blocks.

kevin: Any distribution numbers for validation time?
taylan: Traces show validator times: median 12ms, p95 ~120ms, p99 ~630ms for complex schemas. That's per-request validation time.

arnold: That seems to explain the p99. The inline schemas are often slightly different per request so compiled-schema cache miss is high. Our validator (ajv) compiles and validates frequently.
maria: Do we have any compiled-schema cache for inline tool schemas?
taylan: We only cache for known model schemas. Tool schemas are customer-provided inline, so we get many unique shapes and low hit rate.

kevin: Proposed mitigations:
- Short-term: enable a fast-path bypass that skips validation for trusted workspaces (config: VALIDATOR_FASTPATH=true) — lowers tail latency but increases risk of malformed tool outputs.
- Short-term: increase tool-router worker pool / concurrency to reduce queueing pressure.
- Short-medium: offload validation to an async validator service; return 202 for heavy schemas and validate out-of-band.
- Medium: add LRU compiled-schema cache keyed by sha1(schema) with size limits and TTL.

support_jane: Customer ok with temporary bypass on their workspace. How do we flip it?

taylan: Command to set env on deployment canary:

```bash
kubectl -n platform set env deployment/tool-router VALIDATOR_FASTPATH=true --record
```

Then restart 1/3 pods for canary. I'll do the canary now.

devops-bot: Deployment started: tool-router v2.3.8-canary by taylan. Pod tool-router-5c9f started.

kevin: Monitoring p99 and error rates for 30m. Roll back if structured outputs are malformed or errors spike.

[30m later]
maria: Canary stable. Observed p99 drop from ~1.9s -> ~220ms on canary traffic subset. No new validation-related errors in logs.

taylan: Next action items:
- Implement LRU compiled-schema cache (owner: arnold, ETA 3 days).
- Prototype async validator path with 202 semantics for heavy schemas (owner: kevin, ETA 2 weeks).
- Add instrumentation: log schema sha1 and cache hits (owner: taylan, ETA 1 day).
- Keep fast-path config gated per-workspace and monitored by support_jane.

support_jane: Customer confirmed latency improvement. Closing escalation for now; will follow up when cache PR merges.

kevin: Filed follow-up ticket INF-2452 for schema cache + async validator. arnold please include benchmarks with nested-schema workload.

arnold: Ack — will run synthetic tests at 200 RPS with nested schemas and include p50/p95/p99.

maria: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
